question: Prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion within about 2 years among ADNI MCI participants, from MRI plus cognitive tests. Same task and population class. The shared channels are MRI and cognitive testing (P-183: T2-map signal/texture, volumes and neuropsychology; P-168: FreeSurfer volumes, neuropsychology and demographics). Allowed differences: label definition (P-183 compares converters at 2 years with participants stable for at least 5 years; P-168 predicts conversion before month 48 among those still MCI at month 24), single baseline vs five-visit input, age range (70-80 vs all), and sample size.

figures.P-183: Ensemble AUC 0.824, reported 95% CI 0.681-0.968; n=40 (18 MCIp, 22 MCIs); 100 random 80/20 splits. This is the best of seven methods in Table 4.
figures.P-168: LSTM AUC 0.93 +/- 0.06 (SD across folds), 10-fold CV, n=347 (77 converters, 270 non-converters). Hanley-McNeil with n1=77, n2=270: Q1=0.8692, Q2=0.8963, SE=0.0206, 95% CI 0.890-0.970.
figures.comparison: Headline figures: P-183's 0.824 lies outside P-168's derived interval 0.890-0.970, while P-168's 0.93 lies inside P-183's reported interval 0.681-0.968. The rule's test is met in one direction only.

matched_figure_check: P-168 reports a result under P-183's conditions: a single-time-point model (index exam only, not the five-visit trajectory) in participants aged 70 or older (n=256, 68 converters) with the same 2-year horizon. That figure is AUC 0.87. Hanley-McNeil with n1=68, n2=188: Q1=0.7699, Q2=0.8095, SE=0.0291, 95% CI 0.813-0.927. It contains P-183's 0.824, and P-183's interval 0.681-0.968 contains 0.87, so the matched figures agree in both directions. P-168's full-cohort single-time-point AUC of 0.90 (CI 0.853-0.947) excludes 0.824, but it is not age-matched; the figure matched on both input and age agrees. The papers' own data dissolve the gap. Condition 3 fails.
performance_validity: Passes condition 5: 0.824 and 0.93 are below 0.97. P-183's n=40 makes its estimate imprecise (CI width 0.29), and its 0.824 is the best of seven methods.
reason: The two studies share the clinical question, the channels and the metric, and the headline gap passes the uncertainty test in one direction only (P-183's own interval contains 0.93). P-168 reports the result under P-183's conditions: a single time point, participants aged 70 or older, the same 2-year horizon. That AUC of 0.87 (derived CI 0.813-0.927) agrees with P-183's 0.824 (CI 0.681-0.968) in both directions, so the matched figures reconcile the pair. It does not qualify.
